To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
children aged 6 to 8 years can be considered as accurate reporters of their dietary intake, at least for the school lunch meal.
children as young age as six can report on their own lunch intake with good accuracy, and teachers can record the same meal but with greater systematic error.
6–8-year old children can accurately self-report their dietary intake at school lunch.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the accuracy of self-reporting in children, and the potential of teacher-recorded dietary intake as an alternative to parent-reported intake.
the validation of dietary recalls in a group of young children.
dietary intake assessment in children, and the results are of relevance to researchers, clinicians and policy makers in the fields of nutrition and public health.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a single self-reported recall is a feasible and valid method to assess dietary intake in young Swedish school children.
children can accurately self-report on their dietary intake at school lunch and that this method is superior to that of teacher-recorded intake.
children can be used as reliable reporters of dietary intake at least for one meal at school, but that teachers are not able to report the same intake with as high accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
children can report on their lunch intake, but that parents are unable to report their children’s intake.
children aged 6-8 years are able to recall their dietary intake at school lunch with acceptable validity.
children can be used to report on their own intake of school meals, while teacher-recorded intake provides an acceptable proxy for the children’s intake.
The main takeaway from our work is that
children as young 6 years of age may provide valid reports of their dietary intake, at least for a single main meal, and may be a useful tool in future research.
young children are capable of accurately reporting dietary intake, at least for the main meal at school, but that teachers are not as reliable.
